sixInheritedRepairObligations.consumerVisibleMechanism: Every non-setup recorder error (recorder:store) is recorded after all packet and raw getter errors. The browser can set it earlier: before the post-handler getters (native-history.js:80-82 vs :93), after capture getters but before bubble getters (:132 vs :134-136), or at any earlier record() call (native-observation.js:80-86). Pre-existing errors are also forwarded by later reads (observation-browser.js:59-61, :85, :149). Because the ledger assigns primary and order by arrival (error-ledger.js:94-101, 120-121), a later stateAfter/uiAfter or read getter failure becomes the thrown primary and serialized chronology is inverted. This confirms Evidence10 claim S10-C1 by independent trace, and the defect also covers capture-phase and pre-read occurrences.
sixInheritedRepairObligations.repairNeeded: At each browser site that sets __nsLifecycleRecorderError, attach an observation position: performance.now() at set time and, inside the action recorder, the packet sequence plus capture/bubble phase. Alternatively, copy the recorder error into the packet at the point where it was observed. Then have assertAndRecordObservationErrors interleave recorder occurrences with packet capture/bubble getter occurrences and raw-read getters by actual position. Setup must remain first and Node document validation last. Do not use a fixed category order.
sixInheritedRepairObligations.title: Order non-setup recorder errors by actual browser observation, not category

sixInheritedRepairObligations.consumerVisibleMechanism: When the public store is found replaced, record() always assigns a new cause:null recorder:store envelope. It does not check for an existing error, unlike native-history.js:81/:135 and observation-browser.js:9/:86/:150. If observer setup failed (:127-129, recursive cause chain), a later store replacement plus any listener-driven record() (:142-152) erases the setup envelope and its cause chain. observation-errors.js:25-27 then treats the failure as non-setup and orders it after getters. With a healthy setup, each later record() also replaces the first, specific store error (for example a count-divergence message set by completePacket) with a generic later one, so the first occurrence is lost.
sixInheritedRepairObligations.repairNeeded: In record(), set recorderReady=false but assign the recorder:store envelope only when no recorder error exists. Alternatively, retain earlier envelopes in an ordered list, so the first actual occurrence and its recursive setup cause chain survive.
sixInheritedRepairObligations.title: Do not overwrite an existing recorder error in record()
Normalize button-guard snapshot failures before document validation
sixInheritedRepairObligations.consumerVisibleMechanism: stageButtonGuard reads __nsReadRootSnapshot (:29-31) and returns stateError/uiError (:57-60), but only stages them raw (:70). It then calls assertDocumentIdentity (:71) and returns the guard (:73) without ever calling recordError for those getter failures. resetGame (controls.js:166-168) and revealHotPotatoAnswers (controls.js:85) continue with no ledger entry for an observed state/UI getter failure. If document binding fails, the later Node validation error is thrown, and the earlier browser getter occurrences never reach the normalized ledger. This seam has existed unchanged since candidate07, so it was not introduced by Correction10, but it is within the N07-07 'ALL observed snapshot failures' obligation.
sixInheritedRepairObligations.repairNeeded: Route the guard through assertAndRecordObservationErrors(evidence, label || 'buttonGuard', guard, {url, documentId, timeOrigin}) after staging the raw guard, so that state and UI getter failures are recorded before document validation and the earliest occurrence is thrown. Wrap the helper in the same recordError/rethrow pattern used in observation.js.

sixInheritedRepairObligations.title: Capture remaining Reveal dispatcher guards in keyboardEligible
sixInheritedRepairObligations.mechanism: keyboardEligible = !isInput && !inGame && !inAction && revealConditionPassed. Reveal keyboard.js:167 (speaker-notes focus), :193-195 (isOverlayOpen rejects Arrow keys), :197-199 (isPaused rejects non-resume keys), the config.keyboard/bindings precedence that replaces system arrow navigation, and reveal.js:595 (no listener when config.keyboard is falsy) are not observed. In a paused or overlay state, the staged navigateSlideKeyboard.focusInfo reports eligible while the ArrowDown/Up/Right sent at :80 is ignored by production, so the poll timeout is misattributed. Secondary: Boolean() where Reveal uses strict `=== false` (:146), and exact tag equality where Reveal uses /input|textarea/i (:166).
sixInheritedRepairObligations.repairNeeded: Add read-only discriminators to the same evaluate: Reveal.isOverlayOpen(), Reveal.isPaused() combined with the resume-key set (including config.keyboard togglePause keys) for the pressed keyCode, the speaker-notes className regex, config.keyboard truthiness, and whether config.keyboard or Reveal.getBindings() overrides the pressed arrow keyCode. Use Reveal's strict `=== false` condition semantics and its tagName regex. Do not force focus or change navigation policy.

sixInheritedRepairObligations.title: Bind the initial slide read to its observed document before early return
sixInheritedRepairObligations.mechanism: The initial current-slide read at :19 is a separate page.evaluate that returns only slideId, with no url/documentId/timeOrigin. When it equals targetSlideId, :21 returns success without validating which document produced it. A replacement between the :7 docDomain read and :19 is therefore accepted, and no raw document evidence is staged for the read that decided the outcome.
sixInheritedRepairObligations.repairNeeded: Read slideId together with url/documentId/timeOrigin in one evaluate, stage it raw, call assertDocumentIdentity, and only then compare it with targetSlideId (the same seam as the poll at :85-105).

sixInheritedRepairObligations.title: Prevent phase-less caller errorLedger items from overwriting authoritative recorded phases
sixInheritedRepairObligations.repairNeeded: In error-exposure.js, only update existing.phase during reconciliation if the caller wrapper provides an explicit, valid item.phase string. Do not allow a fallback or intrinsic err.phase from an unannotated caller wrapper to clobber an already-recorded explicit phase.
sixInheritedRepairObligations.mechanism: In ingestPreexistingErrors, when a caller errorLedger item lacks an explicit phase property, resolveWrapperMeta falls back to err.phase || `${phase}:errorLedger`. If the referenced error was already recorded earlier in the ledger with an authoritative explicit phase (e.g. 'portable:close'), reconcileEntry executes because existing.phase !== p, overwriting the recorded phase with the fallback/intrinsic phase and re-serializing the entry. This regresses the explicit recorded phase on exposure.

On the fallback/rejection path, ingest every relevant cursor-eligible packet's genuine siblings in recorded packet sequence and capture-before-post/state-before-UI order before the outer gate can throw. five09FindingsRequiredRegressions.mechanism: Recursive recording exposes an occurrence's serialization into a retained caller array. Wrapper reconciliation replaces that serialization object, and later identity-based refresh appends the replacement too. Internal occurrence deduplication survives, but caller-visible diagnostics contain two ledger-created records for one occurrence.
five09FindingsRequiredRegressions.required_repair: Keep one stable ledger-owned exposed serialization identity per occurrence, reconciling it without replacing or truncating caller arrays/objects. Preserve identity-based deduplication across unrelated numeric order collisions and complete late-error exposure.

five09FindingsRequiredRegressions.mechanism: Reconciliation assigns the authoritative wrapper phase to the entry, then serializeError chooses err.phase over that phase. Entries and serialized/exposed diagnostics disagree for a genuine Error carrying an intrinsic different phase.
five09FindingsRequiredRegressions.required_repair: Make authoritative occurrence-wrapper phase survive serialization and reconciliation, with frameUrl/metadata retained, while preserving the actual Error reference and caller wrapper unchanged. Do not fix this by mutating the Error's phase or dropping provenance.

two09ChronologyObligations.classification: Unresolved original Native chronology obligation, additional to the five enumerated findings
two09ChronologyObligations.assessment: Already captured native packet getter failures precede a newly detected extraction store-integrity/not-ready failure. The consumer records the outer recorder/not-ready categories first, making the later failure primary and ordering earlier packet siblings after it. Recording snapshots before the subsequent Node document exception is locally repaired, but that narrower repair does not establish complete actual-arrival chronology.
two09ChronologyObligations.required_repair: Retain every independent error, but ingest previously observed packet siblings before a genuinely later extraction store/not-ready occurrence. Respect actual source observation order for other paths too; an earlier recorder-setup failure must not be blindly moved behind later snapshots. Propagate the earliest applicable common-ledger normalized Error, not a category-selected wrapper. Do not invent timestamps or apply a universal packet-first/recorder-first category sort.

Preserve caller arrays/objects and unrelated serialized diagnostics. Never sort independent caller/common-ledger numeric order namespaces into fictional global chronology.
